subject: Unexpected usage stamping on /render API + VAT handling (Invoice 202611)
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shipyard.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Carter <sara.carter@shipyard.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Unexpected usage stamping on /render API + VAT on invoice 202611

Hi Soojin,

We pulled our November invoice and noticed a ~3.7x spike in billed tokens against calls to our /render endpoint between 2026-11-10 03:00 and 2026-11-11 02:00 UTC. Our engineers confirmed we did not change client behavior in that window and our server logs show consistent request counts. Attached is a condensed CSV with request_id, timestamp, path, and response_size from our side.

Specific asks:
- Can you provide the raw per-request metering slice you used to bill us for 2026-11 (token counts, session ids, and any sampling windows)?
- Please explain why the bill is ~45k tokens higher than our observed totals (we've reconciled local logs).
- Also, invoice 202611 lists VAT at 20% (we are EU-registered, reverse-charge applies). Please confirm whether Redwood applied VAT correctly — we can re-send our VAT certificate if needed.

We'd like to put invoice 202611 on hold pending investigation; please advise.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, Shipyard.ai
(attachment: shipyard_spike_logs_202611.csv - text/csv)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shipyard.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:32:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage stamping on /render API + VAT on invoice 202611

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the CSV. I'm opening a billing investigation and have created an internal ticket: https://redwood-support.redwood.ai/tickets/87921.

Quick notes / next steps:
- Marcus (billing ops) — can you pull the per-request metering export we used to produce Invoice 202611 for Shipyard.ai (include request_id, model_variant, token_in, token_out, and meter_window start/end)?
- Lauren (AM) — I've placed a temporary invoice hold; I flagged finance to not collect until we confirm. Please keep Sara posted.
- Alex — please confirm you want us to apply a provisional credit if we find an overcount while we investigate; we can issue a credit memo to be applied to the next invoice immediately.

I'll follow up with an initial analysis within 48 hours.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: billing_hold_notice.txt - text/plain)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shipyard.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Carter <sara.carter@shipyard.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 07:09:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage stamping on /render API + VAT on invoice 202611

Thanks Soojin — yes please apply a provisional credit while you investigate.

Attached: a fuller log export (shipyard_spike_logs_202611.csv) and our EU VAT certificate (shipyard_eu_vat_certificate.pdf). We are based in Germany (VAT DE245678901). The VAT line on the invoice appears to have been charged even though reverse-charge should apply.

A few clarifying notes from our side:
- The majority of the extra billed tokens appear correlated with requests that have a repeated header X-Session-Stamp: true; our hypothesis is that your metering tooling might be double-counting KV cache warm-ups for replayed sessions.
- We noticed one client shipped a background requeue job on 2026-11-10 02:55 UTC that replayed ~5k requests in a short window; those are the only high-rate activity on our side. Our logs show the replayed requests were marked with request.replay=true.

If useful, we can grant Redwood a time-limited S3 access to our raw app logs for the 2026-11-09 — 2026-11-12 window. Let me know a contact and we'll share.

— Alex
(attachments: shipyard_spike_logs_202611.csv - text/csv, shipyard_eu_vat_certificate.pdf - application/pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@shipyard.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:46:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage stamping on /render API + VAT on invoice 202611

Hi Alex / team — thanks for the attachments and the replay context. I pulled the metering export and completed an initial reconciliation. Summary of findings: 

1) Root cause: an overlap in our metering windowing logic for short-lived replay bursts. For a small subset of requests where the client retried with the same session id inside a 60s sliding aggregation window AND the request carried the X-Session-Stamp header, our sampler counted both the warm-up prefix and the replayed request as billable body tokens due to a cache-merge edge case. This produced duplicate token counts for ~4,900 requests during 2026-11-10 02:54:00 — 2026-11-10 03:07:00 UTC.

2) Quantified impact: 42,186 tokens overcounted (billed) for the period above. This matches the rough delta Shipyard reported after accounting for model variant weighting.

3) VAT handling: you are correct — Shipyard provided a valid EU VAT id and should have been treated under reverse-charge. The invoice 202611 included VAT in error because the VAT flag did not propagate from the account-level tax profile into the draft invoice generation for that billing run.

Remediation / proposed resolution:
- We will issue a credit memo for 100% of the overcounted tokens (42,186 tokens converted to USD at the rate used on the invoice) and apply it to your next billing cycle to clear the outstanding balance.
- We'll also generate a corrected invoice 202611 (credit memo + revised invoice) that removes the VAT line and marks the invoice as credit-applied. You should receive the credit memo and updated invoice by end of day 2026-12-04.
- Engineering fix: queued a patch to avoid double-counting on cache-merge with session-stamped replays; patch targeted for 2026-12-05 and will be in the next runtime release.

Action requested: Please reply to confirm Shipyard accepts the credit memo and corrected invoice. If you prefer the credit to be refunded instead of applied to the next invoice, let us know and we'll coordinate finance.

Apologies for the disruption — appreciate the clear logs which made root-cause identification much faster.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference
(attachment: billing_reconciliation_87921.xlsx - application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Best,
Alex
